title: Beyond Transparency: Governing Visibility–Opacity Tensions in Circular Supply Chains
summary: ABSTRACT Circular supply chains are widely promoted as mechanisms of environmental regeneration, yet they generate a fundamental and underexplored operational tension: The same processes that require high levels of material transparency also create strong incentives for strategic information concealment. Circular supply chain research has predominantly emphasized the benefits of transparency and traceability, while adjacent research on alliances, coopetition, and knowledge protection recognizes that firms must also protect commercially sensitive information. What remains insufficiently explained is how this sharing–protection tension becomes embedded in circular supply chain operations, where the same lifecycle and recovery information can be simultaneously necessary for coordination and commercially appropriate. To address this gap, this study examines how firms manage the visibility–opacity tension through operational supply chain management (OSCM) processes. Drawing on a qualitative multiple‐case study of 32 US manufacturing firms and approximately 80 semistructured interviews, we identify three distinct tension‐management logics. Selective disclosure sequencing governs the timing and recipients of information across the partner lifecycle. Boundary‐anchored opacity recurrently reproduces comparatively stable information boundaries through institutionalized access restrictions. Adaptive transparency recalibration involves ongoing adjustment of disclosure practices in response to changing market and regulatory conditions. Collectively, these logics reveal distinct operational implications and trade‐offs that informants associate with different forms of visibility–opacity governance, particularly regarding coordination, protection of commercially sensitive knowledge, and responsiveness to changing conditions. These implications are interpreted as perceived process‐level consequences rather than independently measured performance effects. The study reconceptualizes transparency not as a governance target to be maximized, but as a boundary to be actively managed. For managers, the findings provide guidance on configuring disclosure practices to balance coordination needs with competitive protection. By theorizing disclosure as a processually governed boundary rather than a transparency outcome, this study shifts the information governance problem in circular supply chains from visibility maximization to boundary management.

title: Green Accounting Practices, Corporate Social Responsibility and Corporate Financial Performance: Unpacking the Mediating and Moderating Mechanisms in an Emerging Economy
summary: ABSTRACT: There is, however, discussion of an environmental accounting–firm performance relationship in sustainability finance research, especially in emerging economies where disclosure norms and institutional pressures are significantly distinct from those in developed economies. This study aims to provide a comprehensive empirical analysis on the effects of green accounting practices (GAP) on corporate financial performance (CFP) for non-financial year listed companies on Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) during 2015–2023 period. Based on an integrated theoretical perspective, which is based on Stakeholder theory and Institutional theory along with the resource based view (RBV) literature, the study suggests that corporate social responsibility (CSR) is a mediate chain in converting GAP into positive financial results, and corporate governance quality (CG) is a boundary condition that further intensifies the mediate chain. To deal with the endogeneity issue, PSX-listed non-financial firms data is pooled together to analyze the panel using System Generalized Method of Moments (System GMM) estimator in addition to Baron and Kenny mediation procedure and Sobel–Aroian bootstrapped indirect effects test. Moreover, the moderated Mediation pathway is tested by the help of the PROCESS macro Model 14. Results indicate that both direct and indirect effects of GAP have a significant and positive impact on CFP. More importantly, the quality of corporate governance (QoC) enhances the relationship between GAP–CSR linkage as the better the corporate governance structure, the more benefit that the CSR activities based on the information of green accounting disclosure of companies will bring them, which in turn will yield better financial performance. A sector level heterogeneity analysis finds effects are most prominent in energy intensive sectors. Originality/value of the study is this study: (i) introduces green accounting as a strategic institutional signal beyond a mere compliance mechanism; (ii) formal testing of conditionality of CSR mediation under different governance regimes; and (iii) provides the first multi-year, large-sample GMM based evidence on the above framework in Pakistan. The findings have direct implications for the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP), PSX ESG framework developers, institutional investors, and corporate sustainability managers. Keywords: Green Accounting Practices (GAP); Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR); Corporate Financial Performance (CFP); Corporate Governance (CG); System GMM; Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX); Sustainability Disclosure (SD); Emerging Markets; ESG Integration; Moderated Mediation Model.

title: “Compliance Trap” or “Resilience Anchor”? The U-Shaped Impact of Corporate ESG Performance on Agricultural Supply Chain Resilience
summary: Against recurrent external disruptions and the accelerated transition toward sustainable business practices, this study examines whether corporate environmental, social, and governance performance uniformly strengthens agricultural supply chain resilience. Using panel data for Chinese A-share listed agricultural firms from 2016 to 2025, we construct a resilience index covering resistance and recovery capacity and investigate its nonlinear relationship with ESG performance. The results reveal a significant U-shaped association. At relatively low ESG levels, adjustment expenditure and organizational reconfiguration are associated with weaker resilience, whereas the relationship becomes positive after the turning point. Mechanism evidence further supports three complementary channels involving information flow integration, capital flow guarantee, and management flow efficacy. Further period-based analysis suggests that the estimated ESG–resilience relationship exhibits different empirical patterns across regulatory periods. The findings extend the ESG-resilience literature by identifying a stage-dependent relationship in agricultural supply chains and by clarifying how sustainability-oriented investments can shift from short-term resource pressure to longer-term organizational capability.

title: Building supply chain resilience into oligonucleotide CMC from day 1
summary: “The companies that succeed will be those that treat the supply chain as part of molecule design and CMC strategy...”Jokūbas Leikauskas, Editor, Nucleic Acid Insights , speaks with Mayurbhai Patel, Vice President, CMC and Chemistry Development, Judo Bio, about resilience in the nucleic acid raw material supply chain, the promise and limits of enzymatic synthesis, how conjugation strategy shapes manufacturability, and why supply chain thinking belongs in CMC strategy from candidate selection onward.

title: THE EFFECT OF ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL, AND GOVERNANCE (ESG) PERFORMANCE ON EARNINGS MANAGEMENT: THE MODERATING ROLE OF CORPORATE GOVERNANCE
summary: This study examines the effect of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance on earnings management, with gender diversity on the board of commissioners and managerial ownership serving as moderating variables. The study focuses on companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during 2021-2025 period. A quantitative research approach was employed using secondary data obtained from the London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) database and companies annual reports. The sampleconsisted of 51 companies, resulting in 255 firm-year observations selected through purposive sampling. The hypotheses were tested using panel data regression and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA). The findings indicate that ESG performance does not have a significant effect on earnings management. Furthermore, gender diversity on the board of commissioners does not significantly moderate the relationship between ESG perfomance and earnings management. In contrast, managerial ownership significantlymoderates the relationship between ESG perfomance and earnings management. These findings suggest that the effectivenes of ESG in contraining earnings management depends on the presence of effevtive corporate governance machanisms capable of aligning managers interests with those of shareholders. title: Can FinTech innovate Green Finance? Scrutinising the Platform Ecologies of FinTech for Forest Restoration
summary: Green finance has struggled to make a difference in climate change mitigation.For some, the main limitations lie in scaling and diversifying financial flows and instruments to close the climate funding gap, while for others, green finance is fundamentally flawed as an incumbent-led project that opens new environmental frontiers for accumulation.In response, FinTech has been touted as offering the technological solutions that could both bridge the climate financing gap and disrupt the systemic issues green finance faces.Yet, critical voices question whether FinTech is simply the latest 'technological turn' in a long line of socioecological fixes, designed to reintermediate financial activity onto increasingly powerful FinTech platforms.To assess the potential for Fin-Tech to innovate green finance, we explore a suite of FinTech innovations aimed at enticing, incentivising, and thus mobilising retail consumers to fund tree planting for forest restoration as a means of delivering climate, biodiversity, and livelihood outcomes.Rooted in the award-winning Ant Forest innovation by Alibaba, we document eight subsequent variations of the Ant Forest model by different FinTech firms, who share the same focus on enabling consumer-funded tree plantingbut modify the initial innovation in various ways.By utilising a 'platform ecologies' framework, we reveal that these innovations have delivered significant environmental outputs, with these nine FinTechs collectively financing the planting of over 750 million trees, but that evidence of environmental impact in terms of tree survival and carbon sequestration rates, remains vague.Moreover, whilst these nine FinTechs offer novel green finance solutions, they are also fundamentally driven by platform development to increase users and revenuerather than environmental concern.

title: The Effect of Earnings Management on Environmental, Social, and Governance ( ESG ) Performance in the MENAT Region: The Moderating Role of Corporate Governance
summary: ABSTRACT This study investigates how earnings management (EM) influences ESG performance and whether corporate governance mechanisms shape this relationship. Drawing on agency and stakeholder perspectives, the study examines how managerial incentives and governance effectiveness jointly shape the relationship between EM and ESG performance. Using 13,181 firm‐year observations from publicly listed firms across 15 MENAT countries over 2017–2024 and applying a dynamic System GMM approach, the findings reveal a significant negative association between EM and the Refinitiv ESG scores used as proxies for ESG performance. The analysis further demonstrates that the EM–ESG relationship is conditional on board characteristics. To reduce potential measurement overlap between board‐level moderators and governance‐related inputs embedded in the Refinitiv governance pillar, primary moderation inference is drawn from the environmental and social dimensions. The results reveal heterogeneous governance effects across EM measures and sustainability dimensions. Board expertise is consistently associated with a weaker negative relationship between real earnings management and the Refinitiv environmental and social scores, whereas gender diversity, board tenure, and CEO duality exhibit pillar‐ and EM‐specific moderating effects. These findings indicate that governance effectiveness depends on both the form of managerial opportunism and the sustainability outcome considered. Robustness analyses using alternative estimators and sample specifications provide further support for the principal empirical relationships. By integrating EM, ESG performance, and corporate governance within a unified framework, this study contributes to resolving inconsistencies in prior literature and provides novel evidence from the MENAT region. The findings highlight the relevance of governance mechanisms in shaping the association between earnings management and the Refinitiv ESG scores used as proxies for ESG performance.

title: ESG practices as capability architecture for sustainable finance in emerging market banking
summary: Existing banking research often treats environmental, social and governance (ESG) practices as disclosure, compliance or performance outcomes, with limited attention to how banks build the internal capabilities needed to operationalize sustainability. This study examines ESG integration as a capability architecture in Tanzanian commercial banks, focusing on how ESG-related practices are constructed, connected and used to support sustainable finance in an emerging-market banking system. The study adopted an interpretivist qualitative design based on semi-structured interviews with 17 key informants, comprising 15 senior bank managers and 2 sector-level stakeholders. The data were analyzed using hybrid thematic analysis and supported by documentary triangulation from bank reports, sustainability disclosures and regulatory publications. The findings identify four interconnected ESG capability domains: digitalization capability, financial inclusion capability, green finance capability and ESG governance integration capability. Digitalization and financial inclusion emerge as foundational capabilities that support operational efficiency, service reach and market access, while green finance and ESG governance integration represent more advanced capabilities linked to climate-sensitive lending, risk screening and portfolio oversight. The study contributes to theory-informed understanding of sustainable finance by showing that ESG capability formation in banking operates through capital steering, including credit allocation, risk screening, green lending and portfolio oversight, rather than through direct natural-resource management. It reframes ESG from a reporting exercise into a capability-building process through which banks organize sustainability within financial intermediation.

title: Analysis on the Linkage Between ESG Disclosure and Audit Quality from the Perspective of Corporate Governance
summary: The disclosure of ESG information is gradually shifting from a voluntary practice to an institutional obligation. This has expanded the information border of organisations and has resulted in changes in the structure of corporate governance. In April 2024, the Shanghai, Shenzhen and North Stock Exchanges released Guidelines for Sustainable Development Reports of Listed Companies. In 2025, China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) respectively updated the information disclosure and governance rules, which put sustainable development reports in the required disclosure scope. As of the end of 2025, 1,869 listed companies produced sustainability reports, representing 34.7% of all listed companies and over 70% of total market capitalisation. Of them, 67.3% had built governance structures and 44.0% had defined quantitative targets. In July 2025, the Chinese Institute of Certified Public Accountants released the draft of the "Guidelines for Sustainable Information Assurance" to create a regulatory basis for non-financial information assurance. From the perspective of corporate governance, the relationship between the two is an integrated governance loop, not a one-way flow of information, in three ways: optimising the information environment, changing the governance structure, and implanting the audit mechanism. Information disclosure minimises information asymmetry in audits. The assurance system creates a new layer of supervision for non-financial information assurance. They are mutually reinforcing and together offer an interactive system for governance through transparency and disclosure through auditing.

title: SME Sustainability Performance Through Digital Transformation: The Roles of FinTech Adoption, Digital Resources, Sustainability Orientation, and Green Innovation
summary: ABSTRACT Achieving sustainability performance has become a strategic imperative for small and medium‐sized enterprises (SMEs) as they strive to balance economic competitiveness with environmental stewardship and social responsibility in an increasingly dynamic business environment. Although Fintech adoption is widely associated with improved operational efficiency and financial accessibility, its role in sustainability performance remains insufficiently understood. This study examines the relationship between fintech adoption and digital resources and their contribution to sustainability performance in Malaysian SMEs through the mediating roles of commitment to sustainability orientation and green innovation. Drawing on the Resource‐Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, data were collected from 250 SMEs and analysed using a hybrid Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS‐SEM) and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) approach. The PLS‐SEM results reveal that fintech adoption and digital resources are not directly associated with sustainability performance; instead, their relationships with sustainability performance are fully mediated by commitment to sustainability orientation and green innovation, with green innovation representing the stronger mediating mechanism. The ANN analysis corroborates the PLS‐SEM findings and further demonstrates that digital resources are the strongest predictor of commitment to sustainability orientation, Fintech adoption is the most influential predictor of green innovation, and green innovation is the primary predictor of sustainability performance. These findings support the resource–capability–performance perspective by indicating that the sustainability value associated with digital‐financial resources depends on their alignment with organizational capabilities. The study contributes to the fintech and SME sustainability literature by integrating explanatory and predictive analytical approaches to provide a more comprehensive understanding of digital transformation and sustainability. Practically, the findings suggest that SME managers and policymakers should complement digital technology adoption with sustainability‐oriented strategies and green innovation initiatives to support long‐term sustainability performance.

AI.abstract_translation: 摘要：在日益动态的商业环境中，中小企业（SMEs）努力在经济竞争力与环境管理和社会责任之间取得平衡，实现可持续绩效已成为其战略要务。尽管金融科技（FinTech）采用普遍被认为与运营效率提升和金融可及性改善相关，但其在可持续绩效中的作用仍未得到充分理解。本研究考察金融科技采用与数字资源之间的关系，以及它们如何通过可持续导向承诺和绿色创新的中介作用对马来西亚中小企业的可持续绩效作出贡献。基于资源基础观与动态能力理论，研究从250家中小企业收集数据，并采用偏最小二乘结构方程模型（PLS-SEM）与人工神经网络（ANN）相结合的混合方法进行分析。PLS-SEM结果显示，金融科技采用与数字资源并不直接与可持续绩效相关；相反，它们与可持续绩效的关系完全由可持续导向承诺和绿色创新所中介，其中绿色创新是更强的中介机制。ANN分析印证了PLS-SEM的发现，并进一步表明，数字资源是可持续导向承诺的最强预测因素，金融科技采用是绿色创新最具影响力的预测因素，而绿色创新是可持续绩效的主要预测因素。这些发现支持了“资源—能力—绩效”视角，表明与数字金融资源相关的可持续价值取决于其与组织能力的匹配。本研究通过整合解释性与预测性分析方法，为更全面地理解数字化转型与可持续性作出贡献，从而丰富了金融科技与中小企业可持续性文献。在实践层面，研究结果表明，中小企业管理者与政策制定者应将数字技术采用与可持续导向战略和绿色创新举措相结合，以支持长期可持续绩效。

title: ESG e geopolítica global: como sustentabilidadee governança corporativa moldam relações internacionais
summary: This article examines how Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) criteria influence global geopolitics, with a particular focus on sustainability, corporate governance, and the energy transition. Despite the growing centrality of ESG in financial and corporate domains, its geopolitical dimension and its role as an instrument of international power remain insufficiently explored in the literature. Based on a systematic literature review of publications from 2000 to 2025, the study traces the evolution of ESG from Corporate Social Responsibility to its consolidation within investment strategies, public policies, and global governance frameworks. The article links ESG to the Triple Bottom Line model and the Sustainable Development Goals, while also analysing its relationship with human rights and global supply chains of critical minerals essential to the energy transition. It concludes that ESG goes beyond a purely technical and normative function, emerging as a strategic instrument of governance and geopolitical influence.

title: When the Measure Is Contested: ESG Rating Divergence, Corporate Financial Reporting Behaviour, and the Validity of the Evidence Base—A Systematic Literature Review
summary: ESG rating providers assessing the same firm in the same year reach materially different conclusions. Six reviews since 2024 have synthesised what that divergence does to capital markets; what it does to firms’ own financial reporting and audit behaviour, and to the credibility of research using ESG ratings, has not been reviewed. Following PRISMA 2020, this review identifies studies linking an ESG rating imperfection to a financial reporting, disclosure or audit outcome, pairs bibliometric mapping with a thematic synthesis, and appraises each study for how far its inference survives the choice of provider. Fifty-five studies qualified. Among those whose direction of estimation could be coded, more estimate the effect of reporting on divergence than the reverse, and the disclosure evidence and the audit evidence sit on opposite arms of that distinction, so pooling them as consequences of divergence misdescribes most of them. The apparent conflict between findings that disclosure is associated with more disagreement and findings that it is associated with less can be reconciled once disclosure quantity is separated from disclosure quality. The evidence is almost entirely associational. None of the 46 studies whose design could be assessed attains a low inference risk on the review’s coding, and three do on an independent second coding: a low rating is rare and contested, because the field models divergence carefully and then treats it as exogenous to the reporting with which the same literature finds it to co-vary. A reporting standard for ESG-based accounting research follows.

title: Corporate Governance, ESG and Economic Resilience: Reassessing the Role of Indian Companies During Economic Shocks
summary: Economic shocks, from the global financial crisis to COVID-19, supply-chain disruption, inflation and energy-price volatility, test not only the balance sheets of firms but also the quality of the institutions that govern them. This article asks whether strong corporate governance and meaningful environmental, social and governance (ESG) practices enhance the capacity of Indian companies to withstand, adapt to and recover from economic shocks. Using a doctrinal and qualitative socio-legal methodology with a limited Asia-Pacific comparison, it analyses the Companies Act, 2013, the SEBI Listing Regulations, the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting (BRSR) framework, official documents, corporate reports and international scholarship. The article argues that governance capacity is the principal channel through which ESG contributes to resilience: ESG matters where it is embedded in board oversight, risk management and stakeholder relationships, and matters little where it operates as a reporting exercise. Three Indian episodes illustrate governance failure, regulatory repair and operational continuity, although causal claims remain deliberately cautious. The analysis finds that BRSR has improved transparency but cannot by itself guarantee substantive ESG performance. The article proposes an ESG-Integrated Corporate Resilience Framework for India and a set of regulatory and corporate reforms. For economists and policymakers, the findings suggest that firm-level governance is one component of macroeconomic resilience, though it cannot substitute for sound fiscal, monetary and financial-sector policy.

AI.abstract_translation: 从全球金融危机到新冠疫情、供应链中断、通货膨胀与能源价格波动，经济冲击不仅考验企业的资产负债表，也考验治理这些企业的制度质量。本文追问：健全的公司治理与有意义的环境、社会与治理（ESG）实践，是否增强了印度企业承受、适应经济冲击并从中恢复的能力？本文采用法释义学与定性社会法学方法，并辅以有限的亚太地区比较，分析了《2013年公司法》、印度证券交易委员会（SEBI）上市条例、《商业责任与可持续性报告》（BRSR）框架、官方文件、企业报告与国际学术研究。本文认为，治理能力是ESG促进韧性的主要渠道：当ESG嵌入董事会监督、风险管理与利益相关者关系之中时，它才发挥作用；当ESG仅作为一种报告行为运作时，其作用甚微。三个印度案例分别说明了治理失败、监管修复与运营连续性，不过本文刻意对因果论断保持审慎。分析发现，BRSR提升了透明度，但其本身无法保证实质性的ESG绩效。本文提出了面向印度的“ESG一体化企业韧性框架”以及一整套监管与公司改革建议。对于经济学家和政策制定者而言，研究结果表明，企业层面的治理是宏观经济韧性的一个组成部分，但它不能替代稳健的财政、货币与金融部门政策。

title: PENGARUH GREEN ACCOUNTING DAN CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY TERHADAP NILAI PERUSAHAAN MELALUI KINERJA KEUANGAN
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh Green Accounting, Corporate Social Responsibility terhadap Nilai Perusahaan melalui Kinerja Keuangan. Jenis penelitian ini adalah penelitian kuantitatif. Penelitian ini dilakukan dengan menganalisis laporan keuangan seluruh perusahaan yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) selama periode tahun 2019 hingga tahun 2023. Teknik pengambilan sampel pada penelitian ini menggunakan metode purposive sampling, diperoleh 13 perusahaan yang dijadikan sampel penelitian. Data yang digunakan adalah data sekunder yang diunduh melalui website www.idx.co.id. Alat analisis data yang digunakan adalah software Stata Versi 17. Hasil penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa Green Accounting tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap Kinerja Keuangan, Corporate Social Responsibility tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap Kinerja Keuangan, Green Accounting berpengaruh signifikan terhadap Nilai Perusaahaan, Corporate Social Responsibility tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap Nilai Perusahaan, Kinerja Keuangan berpengaruh signifikan terhadap nilai perusahaan, dan Kinerja Keuangan tidak mampu memediasi Green Accounting maupun Corporate Social Responsibility terhadap nilai perusahaan.

AI.abstract_translation: 本研究旨在分析绿色会计（Green Accounting）、企业社会责任（CSR）通过财务绩效对企业价值的影响。本研究属于定量研究。本研究通过分析2019年至2023年期间在印度尼西亚证券交易所（BEI）上市的全部公司的财务报表来进行。本研究的抽样技术采用目的抽样法（purposive sampling），共获得13家公司作为研究样本。所使用的数据为通过网站www.idx.co.id下载的二手数据。所使用的数据分析工具为Stata第17版软件。本研究结果表明，绿色会计对财务绩效没有显著影响，企业社会责任对财务绩效没有显著影响，绿色会计对企业价值有显著影响，企业社会责任对企业价值没有显著影响，财务绩效对企业价值有显著影响，且财务绩效无法中介绿色会计与企业社会责任对企业价值的影响。

title: The Moderating Green Innovation in the Relationship between ESG and Corporate Profitability
summary: Environmental, Social, and Governance practices have emerged as critical determinants of corporate sustainability, yet their relationship with financial performance remains contested in emerging markets. This study examines how green innovation moderates the association between ESG implementation and corporate profitability among Indonesian publicly listed companies. Utilizing panel data from 127 firms across multiple sectors during 2019-2023, we employ moderated regression analysis to test hypotheses. Results reveal that ESG practices demonstrate a significant positive influence on return on assets, with green innovation serving as a strengthening moderator in this relationship. Specifically, firms combining robust ESG frameworks with systematic green innovation investments achieve profitability premiums averaging 3.8 percentage points higher than peers with limited innovation capacity. These findings contribute to stakeholder theory and resource-based view perspectives by demonstrating that environmental innovation capabilities transform sustainability commitments into tangible financial advantages. The study offers strategic guidance for corporate leaders seeking to optimize sustainability investments and provides policymakers with evidence supporting incentive structures that encourage simultaneous ESG adoption and green technological advancement.

title: A Practical Analysis of Digital Transformation and Supply Chain Governance Jointly Advancing Sustainable Development
summary: As digital technology continues to empower the real economy and dual-carbon policies are fully implemented, traditional extensive supply chain management models in manufacturing can no longer meet the practical demands of green and low-carbon industrial transformation. Issues such as fragmented information across the industrial chain, lagging regulation, and unclear responsibilities directly hinder the pace and quality of low-carbon development in manufacturing. To achieve sustainable development in manufacturing supply chains, end-stage remediation alone is insufficient; the key lies in integrating digital technologies with supply chain governance systems to enhance green development from the source. This paper takes the actual operation of manufacturing supply chains as its research subject, combining field survey data with publicly available industry statistics. Moving beyond single-focused studies on either technology or institutions, it emphasizes analyzing the interplay between digitalization and supply chain governance. The study identifies four core challenges in current industrial transformation: significant disparities in digital capabilities among different market players, lack of unified green governance standards across industries, loopholes in value distribution mechanisms along the industrial chain, and insufficient integration between technology and institutional frameworks. Research reveals that digital technologies can address various technical shortcomings in traditional supply chain governance, while standardized governance systems can clearly define the scope of digital technology application. When working in tandem, these two elements can establish a modern, closed-loop supply chain governance system covering the entire process. Addressing practical industry challenges, this paper proposes several actionable optimization strategies, offering practical theoretical references and real-world insights for advancing green upgrades and building long-term governance systems in manufacturing supply chains.

title: Digital economy, green innovation, and high-quality development of the marine economy: evidence from China’s coastal regions
summary: This study examines the association between the digital economy and high-quality marine economic development using panel data for 11 coastal provincial-level regions in China from 2014 to 2023. Composite indices of digital economy development (DIG) and high-quality marine economic development (MEHD) are constructed, and two-way fixed-effects and panel threshold models are used to examine the overall association and its variation across development conditions. The MEHD index captures selected dimensions of marine economic development and is narrower in scope than a sustainable blue economy. The baseline estimates show a statistically significant positive association between DIG and MEHD under conventional province-clustered inference. Multiple checks also yield positive results, but the association does not reach conventional significance levels after accounting for the small number of regions. Green patent application intensity is measured as the number of green patent applications per CNY 100 billion of regional GDP. The existence of a threshold receives statistical support only at the 10% level. Conditional on the estimated threshold, the DIG coefficients are positive in both regimes, with a larger point estimate in the high-intensity regime. Cross-group tests do not reject coefficient equality across regions, periods, or income groups, whereas the urbanization-group difference is significant under conventional province-clustered inference (p=0.027). With only 11 provincial clusters, the threshold and urbanization findings provide exploratory evidence of conditional differences. The study provides provincial evidence on digitalization and high-quality marine economic development, informing context-sensitive approaches to marine-sector digitalization, green innovation, and regional governance that seek to align economic development with environmental sustainability.

title: Managerial short-termism, ESG decoupling, and digital signaling: environmental governance evidence from China
summary: ESG disclosure has become an important mechanism through which firms communicate environmental responsibility. However, whether reported ESG information reflects underlying environmental performance remains uncertain in transitional institutional environments. Using a panel of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2009 to 2024, this study examines the association between managerial short-termism and ESG disclosure–performance divergence, and further investigates whether observable digital investment conditions the risk consequences of such divergence. ESG decoupling is measured as the gap between ESG disclosure intensity and verifiable environmental compliance outcomes. The results show that firms with stronger short-term managerial incentives are associated with greater ESG disclosure–performance divergence. ESG decoupling is also positively associated with corporate downside risk, and this association is more pronounced among firms with higher levels of observable digital investment. These findings are consistent with the view that visible digital investment may reinforce the perceived credibility of ESG disclosure when environmental performance is not fully verifiable, thereby amplifying the risk implications of ESG decoupling.
